stem: A client has an elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) result. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: LDH is a nonspecific marker that can rise with injury or disease involving several tissues, so the result requires clinical correlation
options.B: LDH elevation uniquely diagnoses one specific cancer
options.C: LDH is useful only for kidney disease
options.D: Any elevated LDH proves acute myocardial infarction

rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories notes that LDH is present in many tissues and can be elevated in numerous conditions involving the heart, liver, muscle, kidney, lung, and blood. It is too nonspecific for diagnosis of cancer and has been superseded by troponin for myocardial infarction assessment. An elevated LDH therefore requires clinical correlation.
educational_objective: Interpret elevated LDH as a nonspecific tissue-injury/disease marker rather than a diagnosis by itself.
source_claim_supported: Supports broad tissue distribution and nonspecific LDH elevation across multiple disease processes.
correction_summary: Removed examples that could imply LDH is a modern diagnostic test for MI and made nonspecificity the exact tested concept.
audit_findings: A matches Mayo interpretation; B-D overstate specificity or obsolete diagnostic use.
